source.title: Eureka-Moments in Transformers: Multi-Step Tasks Reveal Softmax Induced Optimization Problems
source.authors: David T. Hoffmann; Simon Schrodi; Jelena Bratulic; Nadine Behrmann; Volker Fischer; Thomas Brox

record.tranche_reason: Tests train/test learning dynamics on a small algorithmic reasoning task, but the task and reported phenomenon differ from the modular-arithmetic grokking setup.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly distinguishes Eureka-moments from grokking: it describes Eureka-moments as occurring without overfitting, with training and validation loss saturating and then improving together. The reasoning-task figure reports train and test accuracy curves, but does not give numerical curve values. Results on vision, language modeling, and ICL concern Eureka-moments and do not test the specific grokking pattern or the other listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures 'Eureka-moments', a different phenomenon. Training and validation loss plateau together and then jump together, with no overfitting phase. The authors explicitly contrast this with grokking. None of its results measure test accuracy jumping long after training accuracy saturates, or any other version's construct. Grokking appears only in related work and in borrowed settings (weight decay 1, 30% split).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that transformers struggle to learn unsupervised intermediate sub-tasks and then learn them suddenly (Eureka-moments). They trace this to small Softmax-induced gradients for the key and query weights, caused by locally uniform attention. Softmax interventions, with NormSoftmax the most robust, speed learning and transfer to RoBERTa and ICL. They distinguish Eureka-moments from grokking because there is no prior overfitting.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a small reasoning task with a transformer and compares Softmax interventions; it does not reproduce modular-arithmetic grokking or the original grokking measurement setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Attention temperature and normalization affect Eureka-moment incidence and timing; the paper also reports sensitivity to learning-rate schedules and task difficulty.

fits_no_version.finding: On multi-step tasks, transformers plateau in both training and validation and then improve abruptly in both. This occurs on vision tasks and on a single-layer reasoning task, and similar jumps appear for RoBERTa and GPT-2 ICL. Softmax temperature fixes (HT, NormSoftmax) shorten or remove the plateau; for example, the main-dataset Eureka-ratio rises from 3/10 to 10/10 (Tab. 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformers show non-grokking abrupt learning plateaus (train and test together) on multi-step tasks, caused by small Softmax-attention gradients for W_Q and W_K.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight decay, noted as a facilitator of grokking, does not help Eureka-moments and tends to lower the Eureka-ratio: 5/10 with WD 0.5 versus 6/10 without (Tab. 1, A.5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight decay does not resolve attention-gradient-driven learning plateaus in transformers.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The algorithmic-task accuracy results are presented as plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The authors note that transfer from controlled synthetic tasks to real data is an assumption, though they report related results on language modeling and ICL.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's probes, gradient analyses, vision-task results, language-modeling loss curves, and ICL results are not rows here: they concern Eureka-moments or their proposed mechanism, rather than the grokking accuracy pattern or other listed versions.

untested.parts: No modular arithmetic task, no measure of the train-saturation-to-test-jump delay, and no training-set-size sweep.
Weight decay 0.5 is tried on the vision task only as a fix for Eureka-moments. There is no memorization circuit, critical dataset size or ungrokking test.
Slingshot effects are noted only after Eureka-moments; they are not tested as a cause of grokking delay.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' classification and its V1 'challenges' label are not justified. A different phenomenon on a different task cannot challenge V1's claim about modular-arithmetic-style grokking. The study's relevance is only as a contrast case of abrupt learning without a train/test gap.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses a Boolean-style reasoning task, not modular arithmetic; it does not sweep training-set size or test whether delay grows as the training set shrinks.

rows.subject: single-layer transformer
rows.size_stated: single layer, four attention heads; embedding dimension 16
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Softmax attention on the reasoning task; train and test accuracy are plotted over training.

conditions.value: reasoning task: input “a b c d =”; n = 11

rows.measure: training and test accuracy over epochs
rows.note: The figure plots train and test accuracy for the Softmax condition. The authors characterize Eureka-moments as distinct from grokking: no overfitting, with training and validation loss saturating and then improving together.
rows.check: This row measures Eureka-moments: train and test improve together after a joint plateau. That is not V1's train-saturates-first delay. 'Reversed' overstates it, because the study does not report that grokking fails to occur. It reports a different abrupt-learning pattern on a different task. The values are figure-only.

rows.subject: single-layer transformer
rows.size_stated: single layer, four attention heads; embedding dimension 16
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Softmax attention and Heat Treatment (HT) on the reasoning task; train and test accuracy are plotted over training.

conditions.value: reasoning task: input “a b c d =”; n = 11

rows.measure: training and test accuracy over epochs
rows.note: The authors state HT reduces the training steps required for Eureka-moments; the figure shows train and test accuracy curves, without numerical values.
rows.check: This compares the authors' HT intervention to plain Softmax on Eureka-moment timing; it is not a grokking measurement. The Eureka-ratio rises from 3/5 to 4/5 (text, Sec. 5.3). There is no train/test gap measure.
